title: Little Office of the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.english: ℣. The Lord hath given us the bread of heaven:

blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Lauda Sion Salvatorem, lauda Ducem, et Pastorem, in hymnis, et canticis. Quantum potes, tantum aude: quia major omni laude: nec laudare sufficis. Laudis thema specialis; panis vivus, et vitalis, hodie proponitur. Quem in sacra mensa coenae, turbae fratrum duodenae, datum non ambigitur.
blocks.english:
Praise, O Sion, thy Saviour;
Praise thy Leader and Shepherd
In hymns and canticles.
Dare to praise Him as much as thou canst,
For He surpasseth all praise,
Nor canst thou praise Him enough.
A special theme of praise,
The living and life-giving Bread,
Is set before us today.
That it was given at the sacred supper table
To the company of twelve brethren
There is no doubt.

blocks.source: ℣. Panem de coelo praestitisti eis Domine.
blocks.english: ℣. Thou hast given them bread from heaven, O Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Omne delectamentum in se habentem.
blocks.english: ℟. Having in itself all delight.

blocks.source: Ant. Dominus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebatur, accepit panem, et gratias agens, benedixit, fregit, et dixit: Accipite, et manducate: Hoc est Corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradetur: hoc facite in meam commemorationem.
blocks.english: Ant. The Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was betrayed, took bread, and giving thanks, blessed it, broke it, and said: Take and eat: This is My Body, which shall be delivered for you: do this in remembrance of Me.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui nobis sub Sacramento mirabili passionis tuae memoriam reliquisti, tribue, quaesumus, ita nos Corporis, et Sanguinis tui sacra mysteria venerari, ut redemptionis tuae fructum in nobis jugiter sentiamus. Qui vivis, et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, Who in a wonderful Sacrament hast left us a memorial of Thy Passion, grant us, we beseech Thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of Thy Body and Blood, that we may continually experience within ourselves the fruit of Thy redemption. Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Sit laus plena, sit sonora: sit jucunda, sit decora, mentis jubilatio. Dies enim solemnis agitur, in qua mensae primae recollitur hujus institutio. In hac mensa novi Regis, novum Pascha novae legis, Phase vetus terminat. Vetustatem novitas; umbram fugat veritas, noctem lux eliminat.
blocks.english:
Let praise be full, let it resound;
Let the rejoicing of the mind
Be joyful and becoming.
For this solemn day is kept,
On which the first institution
Of this table is recalled.
At this table of the new King,
The new Pasch of the new law
Bringeth the old Passover to an end.
Newness driveth away the old;
Truth putteth shadow to flight;
Light banisheth night.

blocks.source: Domine, spiritus tuus, qui descendit super te in Jordane, illuminet et confirmet nos in veritate. suavissimo de coelo praestituto, esurientes replevit bonis, fastidiosos divites dimittens inanes.
blocks.english: O Lord, may Thy spirit, who descended upon Thee in the Jordan, enlighten and strengthen us in truth. [The source sentence is broken here.] With most sweet [no noun is printed] provided from heaven, he hath filled the hungry with good things, sending the disdainful rich away empty.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O Lord, may Thy spirit, who descended upon Thee in the Jordan, enlighten and strengthen us in truth. [The source sentence is broken here.] With most sweet [bread] provided from heaven, he hath filled the hungry with good things, sending the disdainful rich away empty.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: PDF p.57: the paragraph visibly changes after “in veritate.” to “suavissimo de coelo praestituto”. No noun or antiphon opening is printed there. blocks.source: Quod in coena Christus gessit, facidendum hoc expressit in sui memoriam. Docti sacris institutis, Panem, Vinum in salutis consecramus hostiam. Dogma datur Christianis, quod in carnem transit panis, et in sanguinem. Quod non capis, quod non vides, animosa firmat fides, praeter rerum ordinem.
blocks.english:
What Christ did at the supper,
He expressed [the printed “facidendum” is irregular]
In remembrance of Himself.
Taught by His sacred ordinances,
We consecrate bread and wine
As the victim of salvation.
This doctrine is given to Christians:
That bread is changed into flesh,
And into blood [no subject is printed for this clause].
What thou graspest not, what thou seest not,
Lively faith affirmeth,
Beyond the order of nature.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
What Christ did at the supper,
He commanded to be done
In remembrance of Himself.
Taught by His sacred ordinances,
We consecrate bread and wine
As the victim of salvation.
This doctrine is given to Christians:
That bread is changed into flesh,
And into blood.
What thou graspest not, what thou seest not,
Lively faith affirmeth,
Beyond the order of nature.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: PDF p.58 visibly prints “facidendum” and ends “et in sanguinem” without a subject. The familiar sequence is not substituted for these incomplete words; their uncertainty is now identified directly in the prepared English.

blocks.source: Sub diversis speciebus signis tantum, et non rebus, latent res eximiae. Caro cibus, Sanguis potus, manet tamen Christus totus sub utraque specie. A sumente non concisus, non confractus, non divisus, integer accipitur.
blocks.english:
Under diverse appearances,
Signs only, not realities,
Lie hidden wondrous realities.
His Flesh is food, His Blood drink;
Yet Christ remaineth whole
Under either appearance.
By him who receiveth He is not cut,
Not broken, not divided:
He is received entire.

blocks.source: Sumit unus, sumunt mille: quantum isti, tantum ille; nec sumptus consumitur. Sumunt boni, sumunt mali: forte tamen inaequali, vitae, vel interitus. Mors est malis, vita bonis, vide, paris sumptionis quam sit dispar exitus.
blocks.english:
One receiveth, a thousand receive:
As much the one as the thousand;
Received, He is not consumed.
The good receive, the wicked receive,
Yet [the printed “forte tamen inaequali” has an unresolved construction],
Of life or destruction.
Death is for the wicked, life for the good:
Behold how unlike the outcome
Of the same reception!
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
One receiveth, a thousand receive:
As much the one as the thousand;
Received, He is not consumed.
The good receive, the wicked receive,
Yet with unequal lot,
Of life or destruction.
Death is for the wicked, life for the good:
Behold how unlike the outcome
Of the same reception!
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: PDF p.58 visibly prints “forte tamen inaequali”. The former “lot” silently replaced “forte” with a different Latin reading, “sorte”. That unsupported correction is now bracketed and this previously certified passage returned to pending.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Fracto demum Sacramento, ne vacilles, sed memento, tantum esse sub fragmento, quantum totum tegitur. Nulla rei fit scissura, signi tantum fit fractura, nec status, nec statura signati minuitur. Ecce Panis Angelorum factus cibus viatorum: vere panis filiorum, non mittendus canibus.
blocks.english:
When at last the Sacrament is broken,
Waver not, but remember:
As much is beneath a fragment
As is contained beneath the whole.
There is no division of the reality;
Only the sign is broken:
Neither state nor stature
Of Him Who is signified is diminished.
Behold the Bread of Angels,
Made the food of wayfarers:
Truly the bread of children,
Not to be cast to dogs.

blocks.english: Ant. O sacred banquet, in which Christ is received, the memory of His Passion is recalled, the mind is filled with grace, and [the printed “futura gloriae” has irregular agreement] a pledge is given unto us.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Ant. O sacred banquet, in which Christ is received, the memory of His Passion is recalled, the mind is filled with grace, and a pledge of future glory is given unto us.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: In figuris praesignatur, cum Isaac immolatur: Agnus Paschae deputatur: datur manna Patribus. Bone Pastor, panis vere, Jesu nostri miserere tu nos pasce, nos tuere, ut tuos bona fac videre in terra viventium.
blocks.english:
He is foreshown in figures:
When Isaac is offered;
When the Paschal lamb is appointed;
When manna is given to the fathers.
Good Shepherd, true Bread,
Jesus, have mercy upon us:
Feed us, defend us,
Make us, Thine own, to behold good things
In the land of the living.

blocks.source: Tu, qui cuncta scis, et vales, qui nos pascis hic mortales, tuos ibi commensales, cohaeredes, et sodales fac sanctorum civium. Amen.
blocks.english:
Thou Who knowest and canst do all things,
Who feedest us mortals here,
Make us there Thy companions at table,
Coheirs and fellow citizens
With the Saints. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Panem de coelo praestitisti eis Domine.
blocks.english: ℣. Thou hast given them bread from heaven, O Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Omne delectamentum in se habentem.
blocks.english: ℟. Having in itself all delight.

blocks.source: Ant. Nisi manducaveritis Carnem Filii hominis, et biberitis ejus Sanguinem, non habebitis vitam in vobis. Qui manducat meam Carnem, et bibit meum Sanguinem, habet vitam aeternam, et ego resuscitabo eum in novissimo die.
blocks.english: Ant. Unless ye eat the Flesh of the Son of man and drink His Blood, ye shall not have life in you. He that eateth My Flesh and drinketh My Blood hath everlasting life, and I will raise him up at the last day.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Oremus, Deus, qui nobis sub Sacramento mirabili Passionis tuae memoriam reliquisti: tribue, quaesumus, ita nos Corporis, et Sanguinis tui sacra mysteria venerari, ut redemptionis tuae fructum in nobis jugiter sentiamus. Qui vivis, et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O God, Who in a wonderful Sacrament hast left us a memorial of Thy Passion, grant us, we beseech Thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of Thy Body and Blood, that we may continually experience within ourselves the fruit of Thy redemption. Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Has horas tibi recolo piae rationes Tibi, Corpus Domini, ut confessione Contritus, et prava satisfactione Valeam te sumere cum devotione. Amen.
blocks.english: These Hours I rehearse unto Thee [the words “piae rationes” are grammatically uncertain], unto Thee, O Body of the Lord, that, contrite in confession and through “wrongful satisfaction” [the literal sense of the printed “prava satisfactione,” an uncertain source reading], I may be able to receive Thee with devotion. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: complete PDF p.59 commendation visually compared. The source visibly prints “piae rationes” and “prava satisfactione”. Both are already explicitly marked in English; no silently improved “parva” or “orationes” is supplied. The whole stanza remains pending.

blocks.source: O salutaris hostia! quae coeli pandis ostium, Bella premunt hostilia, da robur, fer auxilium. Uni, trinoque Domino sit sempiterna gloria, Qui vitam sine termino nobis donet in Patria. Amen.
blocks.english:
O saving Victim,
Who openest the gate of heaven,
Hostile wars press upon us:
Give strength, bring help.
Unto the One and Triune Lord
Be everlasting glory,
Who granteth us life without end
In our heavenly homeland. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: At Prime the printed text joins a prayer about the Spirit descending in the Jordan to an incomplete fragment about heavenly bread. The English marks this break and the inferred noun “bread”; it does not substitute the familiar complete antiphon from another office.

At Terce the source prints “facidendum” and omits a subject before “et in sanguinem.” The English retains the resulting incomplete statement rather than inserting the missing words from another edition. The source also prints “forte” at None, rendered by its apparent intended sense “lot.”

The Commendation prints “piae rationes” and “prava satisfactione.” Their wording is retained and the uncertainty is marked directly in the English. This passage requires source correction before use as a continuous translated prayer.

10 October 2026: all three complete rendered PDF pages and all 71 passages compared, including introductory attribution, seven hours, hymn continuations across pages, Commendation, local Prime response variant and all same-office reference expansions. Prime’s “Omnem suavitatem etc.” remains abbreviated and is not replaced by the Matins response. Five source-blocked passages are identified directly in English. The source is unchanged; earlier unmarked repairs are archived. Office remains pending.
